Official name: German Bight western approach
Identity note: Named in IMO COLREG.2/Circ.59 (MSC 83, 2007) as amended scheme with special provisions for the North Hinder to German Bight tanker route, implemented 1 May 2008 (S1); listed in IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4). German statute designates it a deep-water route (Tiefwasserweg) mandatory for large tankers (S6 Nr. 6). MSC 109 adopted a revised containership recommendation covering it from 1 July 2025 (lead S5). No evidence of renaming or restructuring by recent IMO amendments was found.
VTS basis: AnlBV Anlage Nr. 3.1 requires ships approaching the Inner German Bight from the west to report to 'German Bight Traffic' at 007° 10' E 'unabhängig davon, ob das Verkehrstrennungsgebiet German Bight Western Approach benutzt wird' (S6); Nr. 5.1 states traffic is monitored under maritime traffic safety. Coverage evidenced for the eastern part of the scheme and its approach into the Inner German Bight; the western extent of the scheme relative to the VTS area was not verified.
Reporting basis: National mandatory report (AnlBV Nr. 3.1) at 007° 10' E for ships and tows over 300 GT, expressly regardless of use of this TSS (S6). Not an IMO-adopted SRS.
Applicability notes: Report: over 300 GT. Mandatory use of the TSS (AnlBV Nr. 6): oil tankers over 10,000 GT, NLS Z tankers over 10,000 GT, NLS X/Y tankers over 5,000 GT, gas tankers over 10,000 GT approaching or leaving the Inner German Bight from the west. Mandatory route for tankers from North Hinder to the German Bight applies to oil tankers 10,000 GT and over, chemical/NLS tankers 5,000 GT (X/Y) or 10,000 GT (Z) and over, and gas carriers 10,000 GT and over (S1, annex 4). Reports under AnlBV Anlage Nr. 3.1 and SeeSchStrO section 58 are made to German Bight Traffic, a VTS. Recorded under the service as VTS reporting duties (national statute, not an IMO-adopted scheme).
Complexity reason: National mandatory reporting plus national mandatory-use rule, IMO mandatory tanker route and 2025 containership recommendation overlap; cross-border Dutch/German routeing context.
Open questions: Exact westward extent of the scheme and whether any part lies in Netherlands waters not verified. IMO text of the 2024 containership recommendation (MSC 109) not retrieved. No evidence found of any recent IMO renaming of German TSS, but Circ. texts after 2016 were not all retrieved.

Official name: Elbe approach
Identity note: Listed as 'Elbe approach' in IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and the Transportstyrelsen 2017 list of IMO schemes (S4). Adopting and latest amending circular not retrieved.

Coverage is of the direct approach; the TSS lanes themselves are in the Inner German Bight covered by German Bight Traffic, but the exact TSS-to-sector boundary was not verified.
Reporting basis: SeeSchStrO § 58 position report at NGN (008° E) to Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic inbound and German Bight Traffic outbound (S7); AnlBV Nr. 3.1 entry report for ships entering the Inner German Bight from west or north (S6). National, not IMO.
Applicability notes: SeeSchStrO § 58: vessels of 50 m LOA or more and ships under § 30(1). AnlBV: over 300 GT. SeeSchStrO section 58 reports on the Elbe approach are made to the VTS centres. Recorded under the service as VTS reporting duties. Reports under AnlBV Anlage Nr. 3.1 and SeeSchStrO section 58 are made to German Bight Traffic, a VTS. Recorded under the service as VTS reporting duties (national statute, not an IMO-adopted scheme).

Official name: Jade approach
Identity note: Listed as 'Jade approach' in IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4). WSV describes it as the link between Terschelling-German Bight and the Western Approach giving access to Weser and Jade from the north (S11). German statute places a pilot transfer position 'im Verkehrstrennungsgebiet Jade Approach' within the Inner German Bight (S6 Nr. 8).
VTS basis: AnlBV Nr. 8 locates the scheme in the Inner German Bight outside the territorial sea; Nr. 5.1 states traffic there is monitored under maritime traffic safety and Nr. 3.1 routes reports to German Bight Traffic (S6). German Bight Traffic monitors the inner German Bight from Borkum to Helgoland (S8).
Reporting basis: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 report at 54° 20' N or 007° 10' E; SeeSchStrO § 58 entry report at 54° 15' N west of Helgoland to German Bight Traffic (S6, S7).
Applicability notes: AnlBV: over 300 GT. SeeSchStrO § 58: 50 m or more. Compulsory pilotage from the Jade Approach transfer position for large tankers, bulk carriers and other ships per AnlBV Nr. 8 (S6). Reports under AnlBV Anlage Nr. 3.1 and SeeSchStrO section 58 are made to German Bight Traffic, a VTS. Recorded under the service as VTS reporting duties (national statute, not an IMO-adopted scheme).
Complexity reason: National reporting, VTS and offshore pilotage obligations combine; single VTS.
Open questions: Adopting IMO instrument and any recent amendments not retrieved.

Official name: Terschelling-German Bight
Identity note: Amended by COLREG.2/Circ.59 (MSC 83, implemented 1 May 2008) (S1); listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4). MSC 109 containership recommendation from 1 July 2025 (lead S5).
VTS basis: Bekanntmachung 19.1.4 and 19.1.5 require vessels using the TSS 'Terschelling - German Bight' and its inshore traffic zone to report to German Bight Traffic at Borkumriff buoy (VHF 79) and at TG 17/C eastbound (VHF 80) (S7). This establishes coverage of the German (eastern) part only. For the Dutch part: No Dutch VTS was found whose defined area covers this offshore scheme. The Netherlands Coastguard performs Vessel Traffic Monitoring (VTMon) and distinguishes VTS as provided by traffic centres (S14, S15); VTMon is recorded as a lead only, not as a VTS.
Reporting basis: SeeSchStrO § 58 entry and position reports (vessels 50 m or more) and AnlBV Nr. 3.1 (over 300 GT) apply on the German part (S6, S7). National, not IMO. No mandatory reporting identified for the Dutch part.
Voluntary reporting: Netherlands Coastguard broadcasts wave-height advice for container ships in TSS Terschelling-German Bight and may advise the northern route; advice is not binding (S13).
Applicability notes: Mandatory route for tankers from North Hinder to the German Bight applies to oil tankers 10,000 GT and over, chemical/NLS tankers 5,000 GT (X/Y) or 10,000 GT (Z) and over, and gas carriers 10,000 GT and over (S1, annex 4). Coastguard advice targets container ships 100 to 200 m at 3 m waves and over 200 m at 4 m waves (S13). Reports under AnlBV Anlage Nr. 3.1 and SeeSchStrO section 58 are made to German Bight Traffic, a VTS. Recorded under the service as VTS reporting duties (national statute, not an IMO-adopted scheme).
Complexity reason: Cross-border scheme: German VTS and national reporting on eastern part, no VTS evidenced on Dutch part, plus mandatory tanker route and containership advice.
Open questions: Exact boundary between German Bight Traffic coverage and the Dutch part not verified. Rijkswaterstaat Brandaris (Terschelling) VTS designation could not be read (officielebekendmakingen.nl returned HTTP 403); search snippets indicate its area is the Terschelling zeegat approach, not the TSS.

Official name: In the approaches to IJmuiden
Identity note: New scheme adopted by MSC 91 and circulated as COLREG.2/Circ.64 (2012), implemented 1 August 2013, per Transportstyrelsen list (S4); associated precautionary areas in SN.1/Circ.317 (S4). Separate IMO deep-water route leading to IJmuiden listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27). Circ.64 text not retrieved.
VTS basis: VTS North Sea Canal Area covers 'the approaches to IJmuiden ... within a 12-nautical-mile radius ... including the extended IJ-geul deep water channel' (S12). The source does not state that the TSS lanes lie within this area; the extended IJ-geul is a separate IMO deep-water route. VTS named as a strong lead; overlap with the TSS needs chart verification.
Reporting basis: No IMO or national mandatory reporting system specific to the TSS found. Within the VTS area there are ordinary VTS reporting duties: report on arrival at 12 nm to Sector IJmuiden VHF 61 and to IJmuiden Approaches VHF 07 'as soon as VHF contact is possible' (S12). These are VTS reporting duties, recorded separately.
Applicability notes: VTS reporting and listening watch apply to vessels in the VTS area per S12.
Complexity reason: TSS, deep-water route, precautionary areas and a port VTS with sector structure; overlap to be confirmed.
Open questions: Retrieve Circ.64 annex or chart INT 1418 to test whether any TSS lane lies within 12 nm of the breakwaters or on the extended IJ-geul. Dutch 2020 to 2023 Notices to Mariners (defensie.nl) returned 404.

Official name: Off Ushant
Identity note: Amended by COLREG.2/Circ.51 (MSC 75), implemented 1 May 2003 (S18); further amended by COLREG.2/Circ.64 (MSC 91), implemented 1 June 2013 per search result (Circ.64 text not retrieved). French ministry 2024 confirms DST Ouessant under CROSS Corsen (S19).
VTS basis: IMO MSC.52(66): OUESSREP area 'covers a circular area 35 miles in radius centred on the Ile d'Ouessant' and 'The TSS covers the entire area'; shore authority is the Corsen/Ouessant VTS 'Ushant Traffic' at CROSS Corsen, VHF 13 (S16). French ministry 2024: 'DST Ouessant : zone de compétences CROSS Corsen' (S19).
Reporting basis: OUESSREP, IMO-adopted SOLAS mandatory ship reporting system (MSC.52(66), amended MSC.251(83) in force 1 May 2008) covering the TSS (S16, S17); French 2024 publication confirms Channel CROSS monitor ships over 300 UMS 'soumis à un compte rendu obligatoire' (S19).

Complexity reason: Single VTS with IMO mandatory reporting; well documented.
Open questions: A current CROSS Corsen or Premar Atlantique page with VHF channels was not retrieved; channels are from the 1996 IMO text.

Official name: Off Finisterre
Identity note: Originally adopted by A.767(18) (cited in S20); amended by A.957(23), implemented 1 June 2004, adding lanes for ships carrying dangerous or pollutant cargoes in bulk (S21). Listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27).
VTS basis: MSC.63(67): FINREP area 'includes the traffic separation scheme "off Finisterre"' and ships 'shall report to the Finisterre Traffic VTS' (S20). The amended 2004 outer southbound lane reaches 010° 13.7' W (S21), slightly west of the 1996 FINREP limit (010° 10' W), so coverage of the outermost lane is not evidenced.
Reporting basis: FINREP, IMO-adopted mandatory SRS in force 3 June 1997 (S20).
Applicability notes: FINREP: ships of 50 m LOA or more; ships carrying hazardous or potentially polluting cargo; tows over 50 m; smaller vessels fishing in or using lanes in emergency (S20). Dangerous cargo ships use designated outer lanes (S21).
Complexity reason: VTS with IMO mandatory reporting; cargo-based lane allocation; possible mismatch of FINREP limit with amended TSS.
Open questions: Salvamento Marítimo website returned HTTP 503/TLS failure, so current VTS name and VHF channel not confirmed from operator; only a 2025 news lead (S22). Check whether FINREP geographical limits were amended after 2004.

Official name: Off Cape Roca
Identity note: Amended by MSC 79 (December 2004) with entry into force 1 July 2005 (S23 preamble) and again by COLREG.2/Circ.61 (MSC 87), implemented 1 December 2010 (S26). Established in Portuguese law as 'EST do cabo da Roca' (S23 art. 4).
VTS basis: DL 263/2009 art. 6 defines the coastal VTS area (west limit 10° 14' W north of 38° 41' N) and art. 10(4) gives the CCTMC supervision of 'regras aplicáveis aos esquemas de separação de tráfego' (S24); DL 198/2006 art. 9 assigns TSS enforcement to the national VTS authority (S23). All Circ.61 positions of the scheme (westmost 010° 13.78' W) fall inside the statutory VTS area on coordinate comparison (S26).
Reporting basis: COPREP (MSC.278(85), in force 1 June 2009) area bounded west by 010° 14' W and to the south-west by the line 38° 41' N 010° 14' W to 36° 30' N 009° 35' W (S25); the scheme lies inside on coordinate comparison. Reports to Roca Control.
Voluntary reporting: COPREP invites any other vessel type to participate voluntarily (S25).
Applicability notes: COPREP and VTS: ships of 300 GT or above, dangerous/polluting cargo, passenger ships, tows over 100 m, fishing vessels 24 m or more (S24, S25). Separate lanes for ships carrying dangerous or pollutant cargoes in bulk (S26).
Complexity reason: Single national coastal VTS with IMO mandatory reporting and cargo-based lanes.
Open questions: DL 263/2009 cites IPTM; current operating authority (DGRM) not confirmed from a DGRM page. Coverage relies on coordinate comparison.

Official name: Western Traffic Separation Scheme (between Grand Canary and Tenerife), part of the Canary Islands schemes
Identity note: New scheme adopted by MSC 81 in COLREG.2/Circ.57 (26 May 2006), implemented 1 December 2006 (S28). Listed as 'Between Grand Canary and Tenerife' in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27).
VTS basis: No designated VTS found. Primary sources name MRCC Tenerife as recipient of voluntary TSS notifications and CANREP reports (S28, S29), but describe it as an MRCC, not a VTS. MRCC recorded as lead (SVC-es-canarias-mrcc).
Reporting basis: CANREP area is a polygon along the outer limit of the territorial sea enclosing the archipelago, so inter-island waters including this scheme lie inside (S29, section 2.1). Applies only to specified heavy-oil tankers.
Voluntary reporting: Ships may notify entry to and departure from the TSS via MRCC Tenerife on VHF 16 (S28).
Applicability notes: CANREP: tankers of 600 dwt and above carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil, bitumen or tar, transiting or trading inter-island (S29).
Complexity reason: Narrow-scope IMO mandatory reporting plus voluntary TSS notification; no VTS.
Open questions: Check whether Salvamento Marítimo operates a VTS function for the Canary TSS (website unavailable). CANREP coverage of the TSS rests on the polygon description; the chartlet was not inspected.

Reporting basis: Inside the CANREP polygon (S29); ships entering east of 015° 30' W report to MRCC Las Palmas.
Voluntary reporting: Ships may notify entry to and departure from the TSS via MRCC Las Palmas on VHF 16 (S28).
Applicability notes: CANREP: as TSS-0064.

Official name: In the Strait of Gibraltar

Open questions: Lead (news/petition, not primary) that Tarifa Tráfico functions were moved provisionally to CCS Algeciras; not verified because salvamentomaritimo.es returned HTTP 503. Current VHF channels should be rechecked against the latest ALRS/Spanish NtM.

Open questions: Confirm centre name (CCS Almería), call sign and VHF channel from Salvamento Marítimo (site returned HTTP 503) or ALRS Vol 6.
Audit adjustments at merge: reporting_finding: Confirmed absent -> Unresolved. Absence rests on a Ministry of Transport magazine article, not a formal complete list. Record the voluntary Cabo de Gata system; confirm absence of mandatory reporting against ALRS Vol 6 or IMO SN.1/Circ.

Official name: Strait of Istanbul

Complexity reason: Montreux Convention regime, national mandatory reporting layered on IMO recommendatory rules, one-way traffic and pilotage rules, multiple linked schemes.

Source label: In Puget Sound and approaches in Haro Strait, Boundary Pass and in the Strait of Georgia

Identity note: IMO name as amended by COLREG.2/Circ.55 (MSC 79, 15 December 2004; amendments implemented 1 July 2005). US statutory text splits it into 33 CFR 167.1320-1323 (Puget Sound and its approaches) and 167.1330-1332 (Haro Strait, Boundary Pass, Strait of Georgia). Grouped heading; the separate Strait of Juan de Fuca and approaches schemes (33 CFR 167.1300/1310) are not part of this label.
Components: Rosario Strait; Approaches to Puget Sound other than Rosario Strait; Puget Sound; Haro Strait and Boundary Pass; Strait of Georgia
VTS basis: US parts: 33 CFR 161.55 defines the VTS Puget Sound area as US navigable waters of the Salish Sea to the US/Canada boundary, and Table 161.12(c) assigns Seattle Traffic Ch 14 (Puget Sound) and Ch 5A (US Salish Sea incl. Rosario Strait and US side of Haro Strait). Canadian parts: CCG RAMN 2026 Table 3-1 places Canadian waters through Haro Strait, Boundary Pass and the Strait of Georgia in Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1 (Victoria Traffic Ch 11). Both operate within the US/Canadian CVTS; the CVTS northern limit is 49°N, so the Strait of Georgia component north of 49°N is a Canadian-only VTS area.
Reporting basis: No IMO-adopted (SOLAS V/11) mandatory ship reporting system found for this area. 33 CFR 161 VMRS reporting (sailing plans, position and final reports) applies, but it is the ordinary participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the service, not as a separate reporting system. A failed search does not establish absence. Canadian side: Vessel Traffic Services Zones Regulations (SOR/2025-275, replacing SOR/89-98) require sailing plans, including a 24-hour report when entering from outside Canadian waters; again VTS participation reporting.
Applicability notes: US: VMRS users per 33 CFR 161.16 (power-driven 40 m+, towing vessels 8 m+, passenger vessels certificated for 50+). Eastern San Juan Island Archipelago VTS Special Area rules (Rosario Strait) for vessels 100 m+ / 40,000 DWT+. Canada: vessels 300 GT+, tows 500 GT+ combined, pollutant/dangerous goods carriers; some provisions also to vessels 20 m+ (RAMN s3.5.1).
Complexity reason: Cross-border grouped scheme under two national VTS regimes within the CVTS, with sector-specific frequencies and a VTS Special Area.
Open questions: Confirm whether 33 CFR 161.55 reference to a Vancouver centre is obsolete (RAMN 2026 lists Victoria Traffic only). SOR/2025-275 full text not fetched (only the SOR/89-98 repeal note).

Source label: In the Bay of Fundy and approaches
Official name: In the Bay of Fundy and Approaches
Identity note: Listed by CCG NOTMAR as a compulsory Canadian routeing system adopted by IMO (ref. charts 4010, 4011, 4012, 4116). Original scheme adopted early 1980s (not effective before 1 June 1983); amended MSC 76 (COLREG.2/Circ.52, 6 Jan 2003), implemented 0000 UTC 1 July 2003; amended scheme has two parts.
Components: Part I; Part II
VTS basis: Bay of Fundy Local Eastern VTS Zone (SOR/2025-275 Sch. 3 item 7). RAMN Part 3 calling-in points for 'Fundy Traffic' include 'Southwest entrance to traffic separation scheme' (1A/1B), entrance/exit (4E) and north exit/entrance (5A/5B), so the TSS lies within the zone.
Reporting basis: SOR/2025-275 Part 4 (Local Eastern VTS Zones): sailing plan 24 h before entry from outside Canadian waters, sailing plan 15 min before entry, position reports at calling-in points, final and deviation reports. National mandatory reporting (successor to ECAREG/SOR/89-99), not IMO-adopted.
Applicability notes: Applies to vessels of 300 GT or more, tow/push combinations of 500 GT or more, and vessels carrying pollutants or dangerous goods; Part 4 reports also apply to vessels of 20 m or more (excluding pleasure craft under 30 m and small fishing vessels) and certain tows. Canadian modification to COLREG Rule 10 requires power-driven vessels over 20 m to use the scheme. Reporting under the Canadian Vessel Traffic Services Zones Regulations (SOR/2025-275) is the reporting duty of the VTS zone. Recorded under the Fundy Traffic and Canso Traffic services.
Complexity reason: Two-part compulsory scheme inside a three-sector VTS zone with statutory reporting.
Open questions: Part of the approach near the Canada/US boundary: confirm whether any TSS portion lies in US waters outside the zone.

Identity note: Listed by CCG NOTMAR as a compulsory Canadian routeing system adopted by IMO (ref. charts 4013, 4233, 4301, 4321, 4335, 4374). Amended MSC 83 (COLREG.2/Circ.59), implemented 0000 UTC 1 May 2008; three parts.
Components: Part I; Part II; Part III
VTS basis: Strait of Canso and Eastern Approaches Local Eastern VTS Zone (SOR/2025-275 Sch. 3 item 5), bounded seaward by the territorial sea limit. Reporting basis: SOR/2025-275 Part 4 Local Eastern VTS Zone reporting (24 h pre-entry sailing plan from outside Canadian waters, 15 min pre-entry sailing plan, calling-in-point position reports, final reports). National mandatory, not IMO-adopted.
Applicability notes: As for Bay of Fundy (SOR/2025-275 ss 3 and 24). Parts of the TSS seaward of the territorial sea limit may fall within the Eastern VTS Zone (Schedule 2) instead.
